metadata.capability_extraction: Can inspect visual desktop state; VLC is open and accessible for modifying interface and playback settings.
metadata.explanation: Task asks user to disable the 'Use only one instance when started from file manager' option in VLC via Tools > Preferences > Interface. Evaluator kills VLC (forces config save), reads ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc and checks one-instance-when-started-from-file=0. The default is 1 (enabled), so initial state will not pass negative control check.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires disabling 'only one instance when opening a file' in VLC settings, which maps directly to the config key 'one-instance-when-started-from-file=0' in ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc.
Postconfig correctly kills VLC before reading config, ensuring settings are flushed/persisted to disk before the getter reads the file.
Getter 'get_vlc_config' reads the correct VLC config file (~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux) and returns its path.

Metric 'check_one_instance_when_started_from_file' scans for the correct config key and compares to expected value '0'. Parameter handling is correct: rule dict is accessed directly as rule['expected_one_instance_when_started_from_file'].
Default fallback in metric is '1' (enabled by default), so the initial state correctly fails the check — good negative-control resistance.
Expected value '0' is semantically correct for 'turning off' the option.

Minor: The metric does not skip commented lines (e.g., '#one-instance-when-started-from-file=1' would also match the substring). However, since the loop processes all lines and the last match wins, and VLC writes the active setting after commented defaults, this is unlikely to cause failures in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional hardening: skip commented lines in check_one_instance_when_started_from_file by adding 'if line.startswith("#"): continue' to avoid any edge-case match on commented defaults.
